Architecture Diagram

The application is a server-rendered catalog web application with a single ASP.NET MVC deployment. Catalog persistence and image storage are abstracted behind services, with optional Azure integrations.

Data Storage & External Services

Catalog records are stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6, with LocalDB configured for local execution and a mock catalog option. Images can use Azure Blob Storage or the local Pics directory. Azure Active Directory sign-in and Application Insights instrumentation are optional integrations selected through configuration.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Controllers depend on ICatalogService and IImageService; Autofac selects database/mock and Azure/local implementations from configuration.
  • Entity Framework's CatalogDBContext is the persistence boundary; there is no separate repository layer.
  • The web application is a single deployable unit; database and cloud storage are external resources.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is the catalog domain entity used by the create/edit form and catalog views; CatalogBrand and CatalogType are related service-level entities. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the page response model. The image upload accepts a multipart file and returns an anonymous JSON object with name and url properties. No immutable request/response DTOs, OpenAPI document, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema were found. MVC Razor rendering and MVC JSON serialization are used.

Communication Patterns

Controllers call local catalog and image service interfaces synchronously. The database implementation uses Entity Framework 6 against SQL Server; the alternative catalog implementation uses an in-memory list. Image uploads use synchronous Azure Blob Storage operations when Azure storage is enabled, otherwise the mock/local implementation is selected. There is no message broker, service discovery, API gateway, circuit breaker, or retry policy identified.

Azure AD OpenID Connect is optional. In the non-Azure-AD path, custom middleware creates a claims identity for the request. Catalog create, edit, and delete actions have [Authorize]; the image-upload action has no visible authorization attribute. The project configures an IIS Express development SSL port, while the Dockerfile exposes HTTP port 80; no application-wide TLS enforcement was found.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. Compose starts the sql.data service before the web app through depends_on; no readiness wait is declared in the base Compose file.
  2. The MVC application starts and registers Autofac, routes, filters, and bundles.
  3. When database mode is active, Entity Framework's database initializer creates the database/sequences and seeds catalog data.
  4. Catalog image initialization runs before the OWIN pipeline is initialized; Azure storage may be contacted when that mode is enabled.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining a product catalog, including product classification, inventory thresholds, and product images. It is a single catalog bounded context with no cross-service business orchestration.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct offered in the catalog with price, stock, reorder thresholds, and image referenceBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification for catalog itemsHas many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementProduct type/category classificationHas many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server/LocalDB or in-memory mock; optional Azure Blob Storage

Catalog data is owned by the MVC application and persisted through its Entity Framework context. No service-to-service calls, shared cross-context identifiers, or event-based data exchange were found.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog index.
  2. CatalogController requests the selected page from ICatalogService.
  3. CatalogService loads catalog items and related brand/type data from Entity Framework, or the mock service reads its in-memory list.
  4. The controller sets image URLs and renders the paginated catalog view.

Workflow 2: Create or Update a Catalog Item

  1. An authorized user opens the create or edit form and supplies catalog, price, inventory, and optional image information.
  2. MVC model validation checks required name, price format/range, and inventory threshold ranges.
  3. On valid create, the catalog service assigns an identifier and saves the item; if a temporary image is supplied, the image service moves/copies it to the item location.
  4. On valid edit, an optional image is updated, then the catalog record is saved.
  5. The user is redirected to the catalog index. Invalid models are returned to the form.

Workflow 3: Upload a Product Image

  1. The client posts a multipart image to /uploadimage with an optional catalog item identifier.
  2. PicController decodes the stream and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats.
  3. The image service stores the temporary image in Azure Blob Storage when enabled; mock mode returns the default image URL.
  4. The endpoint returns JSON containing the temporary image name and URL for use by the catalog form.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No gateway or cross-service data composition exists. Catalog data is read and written within the same application/database boundary. Image storage is a separate optional persistence resource: the upload endpoint returns a temporary image reference, which the create/edit workflow later uses to associate the image with a catalog item. If Azure storage is disabled, the mock image service supplies a local/default image URL.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Catalog editor" participant Pic as "PicController" participant Image as "Image service" participant Catalog as "CatalogController" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant DB as "Catalog database" User->>Pic: Upload image with item identifier Pic->>Pic: Check image format alt Supported image Pic->>Image: Store temporary image Image-->>Pic: Temporary image URL Pic-->>User: Return name and URL else Unsupported image Pic-->>User: Return bad request end User->>Catalog: Submit catalog item form Catalog->>Catalog: Validate catalog model alt Model valid Catalog->>Service: Create or update catalog item Service->>DB: Save catalog record DB-->>Service: Saved item opt Temporary image supplied Catalog->>Image: Associate temporary image with item Image-->>Catalog: Image updated end Catalog-->>User: Redirect to catalog index else Model invalid Catalog-->>User: Return form with validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item name is required; price must match the configured numeric format and fall within its allowed range.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock threshold are range checked.
  • Catalog items reference an existing brand and type.
  • Create assigns a catalog identifier through a SQL sequence in database mode; mock mode assigns the next list identifier.
  • Uploaded images must decode as JPEG, PNG, or GIF before storage.
  • Entity Framework SaveChanges persists each catalog mutation; no multi-service transaction, saga, or compensating action was identified.
  • Catalog create/edit/delete actions require authorization. Image-upload authorization is not explicitly annotated.
  • Logging records action/request processing, but no dedicated business audit trail was found.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses the legacy packages.config dependency model. Several packages are old, including Entity Framework 6.3.0, log4net 2.0.12, OWIN components, and Azure SDK packages. The .NET 10 upgrade assessment also flags package compatibility and framework modernization concerns. CVE results are documented in the security assessment; the NuGet dependency-tree command could not resolve this classic web project because the runner lacks Microsoft.WebApplication.targets, so this inventory reflects declared packages only.

Notable Observations

  • The project declares 146 packages across the groups above, including 90 runtime, configuration, and framework utility packages.
  • Both Microsoft.Azure.KeyVault and older Azure Storage SDK packages are present; these are modernization-sensitive dependencies.
  • Authentication dependencies include JWT packages as well as OWIN OpenID Connect.
  • No test-scoped package references were declared in this project.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application models a product catalog with three Entity Framework entities and persists it in SQL Server when database mode is enabled. Local mock data and local or Azure-backed images are alternative configuration paths.

Entity Model

Entity definitions are in src/eShopModernizedMVC/Models/CatalogItem.cs, CatalogBrand.cs, and CatalogType.cs. CatalogDBContext configures the table names, keys, required fields, and relationships.

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "brands" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "categorizes" CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type } CatalogItem { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogTypeId FK int CatalogBrandId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder }

CatalogItem has required CatalogBrand and CatalogType relationships. Catalog identifiers are generated from SQL sequences by CatalogItemHiLoGenerator; CatalogDBInitializer creates the sequences and seeds initial records.

Caching Strategy

No application-level cache provider, cache annotations, cache TTL, or query-result caching was identified. The mock catalog is an in-memory data implementation, not a cache of the database.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All relational catalog entities belong to the single web application and share one SQL Server database context. There are no cross-service database boundaries or service-to-service data calls. Images are stored in Azure Blob Storage or served from the local Pics directory, depending on configuration. Catalog reads and writes use the service layer and its Entity Framework context; there is no CQRS or outbox pattern.
